findings.review_scope: Manual registered-source content review of arXiv:2210.17439v2, stamped 12 February 2024. Main pages 1-25 were used, with a heading-only crop of Appendix A on page 26. Appendix bodies on pages 26-66 are excluded. Fresh text evidence is retained for every main-text page; formula and passage pages were inspected as rendered images.
findings.inventory: Exactly five actual main-text Theorem headings: 2.2 on page 8, 2.4 on page 9, 2.5 on page 10, 2.8 on page 12 and 3.5 on page 18. All five complete bodies fit on their respective pages. Remarks, Corollaries, theorem citations and supplement results are not inventoried.
original_statements: Theorem 2.2 retains Assumptions A1-A3, the full rate (2.16), alpha in (0,1-exp(-1)), the uniform-null limsup, strict boundary-count clause and both final cases. The source quantifier ambiguity involving theta under a supremum over laws is recorded separately.
Theorem 2.4 states the dimension-growth condition and power over H_1(c), which imposes only A1. Neither A2, A3 nor the level theorem rate (2.16) has been added.

Theorem 2.5 preserves both terms and exponents in (2.24), both conclusions, the bootstrap-null class definition and the bounded-kernel refinement. Theorem 2.8 inherits that full assumption block, uses its own unstarred absolute statistic, and retains both conclusions and the printed repeated phrase defined in defined in.

Theorem 3.5 preserves the unit-variance covariance specialization, d=p(p-1)/2, both dimension rates, c_0<1-Delta, alpha+beta<1, sufficiently-large qualifiers and the minimax nonrejection inequality. The adjacent test-class definition literally bounds null nonrejection; it has not been silently repaired.
source_passages: All 26 source entries, seven auxiliary passages and 14 source notes were compared with their main-text locations. The iid p-dimensional model, symmetric order-m kernel and d-dimensional expectation parameter remain distinct. The pairwise vectorization uses columns above the diagonal.

The uncentered first projection, jackknife factor and excluded-index sum, normalized squared statistic, Gumbel quantile and normalizers match pages 4-7. A1 retains all three bounds; A2 retains its strict restricted lower bound and empty-minimum convention; A3 retains its correlation sum.

The parameter region V_0 has no distributional assumptions. H_0 imposes A1-A3, H_1 only A1, and H_(0,boot) A1-prime and A2. The stronger uncentered repeated-index bounds of A1-prime are not equated with A1.

The resampled U-statistic, full V-statistic conditional mean, positive-Delta truncation for both outside tails, and normalized/absolute bootstrap formulas match pages 9-12. Inherited assumptions do not introduce an unused variance estimator.

The population covariance and its order-two kernel were checked on page 15, including a magnified crop. The arbitrary-test class and covariance lower-bound context were checked on page 18. Corollary-specific C1/C2 conditions were not imported.
findings.dependency_review: 31 direct uses and 74 deduplicated related connections across 26 interfaces. Checked every direct list and all 26 related-theorem sets. Theorem 2.8 excludes jackknife, squared-test and Gumbel construction dependencies; both bootstrap results exclude A3. The minimax theorem inherits its printed null/alternative classes but does not acquire the U-statistic estimator, jackknife, bootstrap or Gumbel test construction.
findings.names_and_highlights: All entries retain source natural-language keywords and source types. Adjacent naming contexts for symmetric kernel, A1, A2, A1-prime and the bootstrap null were checked. Selectors identify source formulas or labels and occur only in the source or related same-paper statements; mathematical correspondence was checked in addition to string presence.
findings.source_limitations: Original inconsistencies remain separate from quotations: dimension-domain mismatch, quantifier ambiguity, zero empirical variance and correlation domains, Orlicz terminology for beta<1, unsupported null-class inclusion, positive-Delta clipping, starred decision typos, threshold-nesting direction and the minimax test-class nonrejection event. Source review certifies faithful extraction, not correctness of the printed results.
findings.changes: No census-content correction was required. The per-paper rebuild now resolves the fixed local source and reproduces all six extracted artifacts without rewriting the historical audit. Earlier scripts are archived.
findings.validation: The independent inventory and census validators pass. Six rebuilt artifacts match saved bytes exactly. Source identity and these mechanical checks supplement the manual content review; neither alone establishes fidelity.
